question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal.
question.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1+6\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{8}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1+6\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{8}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(8[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
